text:
owen: hi all, rookie mistake incoming. I spun up our docker-compose and postgres immediately exits with: "FATAL: database files are incompatible with server". container logs show: "The database cluster was initialized by PostgreSQL version 13, which is not compatible with this version 15". I'm using a host bind ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data because I wanted persistent dev data. any safe way to recover or should i nuke it?

rachel: welcome! :wave: that message usually means there's leftover data from an older PG major version on the host dir. If you don't need the old DB, `rm -rf ./pgdata/*` (or back it up first) then start fresh. If you need to keep it, you'll have to use `postgres:13` to run migrations and dump/restore, or use `pg_upgrade` which is painful locally.

sam: +1. Quick checklist: 1) verify there's a PGVERSION file: `cat ./pgdata/PG_VERSION` 2) if it shows 13, either run `image: postgres:13` and `pg_dumpall` to produce SQL dumps, then switch back to 15 and restore, or remove the folder.

owen: i do see PG_VERSION=13. i definitely don't need those dev rows, but worried about proper cleanup. any docker-compose way to reset cleanly?

rachel: use `docker-compose down -v` to remove named volumes, but since you're using a host bind, that won't delete ./pgdata. For host bind: `rm -rf ./pgdata && mkdir ./pgdata && chmod 700 ./pgdata` then `docker-compose up`. Might need `sudo` if permissions are funky.

infra-bot: onboarding tip: prefer named volumes for local dev to avoid stale host artifacts from previous projects. See dev-setup > local-db. https://intranet.redwood.dev/dev-setup#local-db

owsam: small extra: if you switch the compose to a named volume temporarily to restore from dump, you can keep host dumps outside of the mount and avoid mixing data directories. Example:
```
# quick flow
# 1. run postgres:13 with host bind to export dump
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)/pgdata":/var/lib/postgresql/data postgres:13 pg_dumpall -U postgres > ../all.sql
# 2. remove host dir
rm -rf ./pgdata
# 3. start postgres:15 and restore
docker-compose up -d
cat ../all.sql | docker exec -i <pg-container> psql -U postgres
```

owsam: if you just want to obliterate it: `rm -rf ./pgdata` then `docker-compose up` and Postgres will init fresh.

owen: thanks. i nuked it after backing up a copy just in case. started with named volume instead and migrations ran. learning: avoid leaving old PG data in host mounts across major upgrades :grimacing:

data-eng: one more note: if you ever see the mismatch on CI, it's often because the CI image changed PG version. We pin in compose for dev to avoid surprises. Happy to help if you hit dump/restore issues.

owen: appreciate it — all green now :tada:
